newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Sun Life upbeat on UK life market.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Sun Life upbeat on UK life market.

text.p: UK insurer Sun Life & Provincial Holdings Plc said on Thursday it was pleased with its first set of results since flotation and was well placed to maximise profits from the recovery in the UK life assurance market.
"We are very pleased with the results," the group's chief executive, Michael Hart, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Earlier the group, which brings together Sun Life, UAP Provincial and New Ireland Holdings, reported pro forma pre-tax profits of 92.5 million stg for the six months to June 30, 1996.
Hart said the UK life market seemed to be recovering, although the sector remained highly competitive.
Sun Life provides life assurance, pensions and investment products to both individuals and businesses in the UK.
Hart said the unit had not had to sacrifice profit margin in order to maintain its market position.
He said UAP Provincial, the general insurance unit, would stand up well in terms of underwriting profit with its competitors. "We think it will stand comparison in the market place," he added.
Motor insurance rates were starting to go up and Hart said he envisaged rises of between two and four percent. "There will be room for some more (increases) later in the year," he said.
Hart said other insurance rates were still very soft. He believed there would be a turnaround, but not before mid or late 1997. The change would take place because margins would be squeezed too much.
But UAP Provincial was not as exposed to rate-cutting as other insurers because it had mainly small ticket business.
He said he did not regard the group as a whole as a composite, and said he did not think it helpful to discuss possible acquisitions in the public domain.
"Obviously as a group we are vigorously looking at the market place, what the opportunities are and what we should be doing in the market," he said.
The group was focussed on shareholder value and would act to make sure that whatever it did had a positive effect on this.
